world.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
world.description: Bassam al-Hassan, linked to reporter Austin Tice's abduction, is being sheltered in return for information.

world.title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
world.description: Israel said in September it would act in response to UK sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

world.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
world.description: A lawyer says the murderer of Colleen Slemmer is moving around her hospital room after surviving two lethal injections.

world.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
world.description: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September.

world.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections
world.description: Lawyers for Jamaal Howard had asked a judge to pause the execution after Christa Pike's botched lethal injections.

world.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
world.description: Pioneering computer scientist led the development of the software for Nasa's Apollo mission and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

world.title: New York court hears arguments in ongoing 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia
world.description: The families allege that men with links to the Saudi government helped those who carried out the 2001 attacks, something the country denies.

world.title: France's school protests: What lies behind the anger
world.description: Students' blockades and marches spring from real grievances – and from France's habit of settling policy on the street.

world.title: Eritrean troops move deep into Ethiopia's Tigray region, residents tell BBC
world.description: Residents of Adigrat tell the BBC they have seen truck loads of soldiers from Eritrea moving south.

world.title: Trump wants a new Camp David-like retreat at his Florida golf club
world.description: Trump's estate would stand in stark contrast to the rustic Camp David and mark another tradition transformed by Trump.

world.title: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro expected to face more charges this week
world.description: The new charges are expected to accuse Maduro and his wife of playing a role in the torture of Americans in Venezuelan prisons, US media reports.

world.title: Asahi and Kirin among Japan beer giants raided over alleged price-fixing cartel
world.description: Japan's Fair Trade Commission conducted searches of the country's largest beer-makers.

world.title: Three people killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia airports, officials say
world.description: The Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attacks, which mark an escalation in the conflict.

world.title: Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar suddenly dies at 75
world.description: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.

world.title: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
world.description: People with mental illness alone were to be eligible for assisted dying in Canada in March 2027, but that has now been paused indefinitely.

US.title: Flock is catching flak. Experts say other police surveillance tools are more worrisome
US.description: Real-time crime-center software is a sometimes overlooked but powerful tool allowing police to aggregate immense amounts of data, significantly expanding their surveillance reach.

US.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
US.description: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

US.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
US.description: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

US.title: Toss-ups, triage and targets: How to read the wide-open 2026 House map
US.description: Both parties are spending heavily in roughly 60 House districts — where Trump won by an average of nine points in 2024 — that could be key to deciding control of the chamber, an NPR analysis finds.

US.title: Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected by U.S. and Lebanon, NPR and BBC find
US.description: A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity is living quietly in Lebanon, bankrolled and protected by American and Lebanese authorities, a BBC/NPR investigation has found.

US.title: Trump proposes Camp David-style presidential retreat at his private Florida golf club
US.description: President Trump said he wants to develop one of his Florida golf courses into a presidential retreat where his successors can spend quiet weekends, describing it as "sort of a Camp David."

US.title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction shook Spain, has died
US.description: María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis, died on Wednesday while hospitalized.

US.title: Isaias strengthens into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season
US.description: The National Hurricane Center said late Wednesday that the hurricane was on track to strike the U.S. Gulf Coast later in the week. It's expected to bring heavy rains and potentially flash floodin

US.title: The WHO seeks more details on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia
US.description: The World Health Organization says it wants more information on what caused the death of an employee at a Russian plague research lab. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

US.title: What is the pneumonic plague?
US.description: The ancient disease of plague is back in the headlines after the death this month of a Russian lab worker.
